hooks.text: Three sides, one message: watch out ahead.

cites.sentence: Triangles warn.
All triangular signs are red.
Red rings or circles tell you what you must not do, e.g. you must not exceed 30 mph, no vehicles over the height shown may proceed.
Blue circles generally give a mandatory instruction, such as ‘turn left’, or indicate a route available only to particular classes of traffic, e.g. buses and cycles only.

hooks.text: Blue box: information, or directions on a motorway.

cites.sentence: Blue rectangles are used for information signs except on motorways, where blue is used for direction signs.

hooks.text: Green guides you along primary routes.

cites.sentence: Green rectangles are used for direction signs on primary routes.

hooks.text: White guides you along non-primary routes.

cites.sentence: White rectangles are used for direction signs on non-primary routes, or for plates used in combination with warning and regulatory signs.

hooks.text: Green panels for primary routes, white for non-primary.

cites.sentence: Green rectangles are used for direction signs on primary routes.
White rectangles are used for direction signs on non-primary routes, or for plates used in combination with warning and regulatory signs.

hooks.text: Warning signs: something ahead needs care.

cites.sentence: There are 3 basic types of traffic sign: signs that give orders, signs that warn and signs that give information.

hooks.text: Order signs aren't advice: do what they say.

cites.sentence: There are 3 basic types of traffic sign: signs that give orders, signs that warn and signs that give information.

hooks.text: Motorway exits are usually signed 1 mile and ½ mile ahead.

cites.sentence: The first 2 signs on the approach to a junction show the destination and the route number for the exit only. The distance shown (usually 1 mile or ½ mile) is the distance to the exit (start of the deceleration lane).

hooks.text: Direction signs: the panel colour tells you the kind of route.

cites.sentence: Green rectangles are used for direction signs on primary routes.
White rectangles are used for direction signs on non-primary routes, or for plates used in combination with warning and regulatory signs.

hooks.text: Information signs tell you about the road ahead.

cites.sentence: There are 3 basic types of traffic sign: signs that give orders, signs that warn and signs that give information.

hooks.text: Road works signs: any works, big or small.

cites.sentence: This sign, indicating road works or an obstruction in the carriageway ahead, may be used for any type of works, ranging from large construction schemes to minor maintenance.

hooks.text: Red ring number: the most. Blue circle number: the least.

cites.sentence: The maximum speed, in miles per hour, at which traffic may travel, if it is safe to do so.
Minimum speed permitted, in miles per hour, unless it is impracticable or unsafe to comply.

hooks.text: National speed limit: it depends on the road and the vehicle.

cites.sentence: The national speed limit for the type of road and class of traffic applies.

hooks.text: Mini-roundabout: give way to the right.

cites.sentence: Mini-roundabout (give way to traffic from the immediate right).
